clue.text: A supporter is upset about minor injury

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment that supports, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the little word is upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: on can mean about, concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: Someone is upset because a backer has a small hurt to complain about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses IS to give SI, so the pieces run A, BRA, SI, ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasion is a graze, a scrape of the skin, which is a minor wound.

clue.text: Occasional Australian turning up in US state

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: Cal. is a short form of California

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the abbreviation reads from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Aus is the standard abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: An Australian who only visits sometimes keeps showing up in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' works because this is a down clue: the Australian abbreviation reads upwards, backwards, before 'in' places it. Cal. is the short form for California.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual work or a casual visitor is irregular, happening only now and then: occasional.

clue.text: Truncated opening feature

indicators.note: truncated means cut short, so the word for opening loses its final letter

parts.note: a chink is a narrow opening or crack

explanation.surface: An opening feature of something, like a film's first scene, has been cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Truncated' cuts the last letter from CHINK. CHIN also belongs to the puzzle's theme: Unsuk Chin is a composer, one of several women composers in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The chin is part of the face, and facial parts are called features.

clue.text: Greek trilogy, trio translated with ease

indicators.note: translated suggests turning words into a new form, so the letters of trio and ease are rearranged

explanation.surface: A set of three Greek plays has been translated without much trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges the letters of TRIO and EASE together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oresteia is Aeschylus's set of three tragedies about Orestes and the house of Atreus.

clue.text: Amassed wealth draws in Welsh director in Hollywood

indicators.note: draws in means takes something inside, so the letter for Welsh goes into the word for amassed wealth

parts.note: a hoard is a store of accumulated treasure

explanation.surface: A rich Welsh film director in Hollywood is pulling in money.
explanation.walkthrough: HOWARD is also in the theme: Emily Howard is a British composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ron Howard is an American film director, maker of Apollo 13 and A Beautiful Mind.

clue.text: Trimmed unnatural river structure

indicators.note: trimmed means cut back, so the word for unnatural loses its last letter

parts.note: weird means strange, unnatural

explanation.surface: Something built on a river looks oddly trimmed and artificial.
explanation.walkthrough: WEIR is a theme answer too: Judith Weir is a Scottish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low dam built across a river to control the flow of water.

clue.text: Whale's time with expert in the sea, nothing less

definitions.note: an adjective, of or belonging to whales, as cetacean is

indicators.note: in places time and expert inside what is left of the sea word
less means without, so the zero is taken out of the word for the sea

parts.note: the ocean is the sea
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
an ace is an expert, someone highly skilled

explanation.surface: A whale spends its time as a skilled performer in the sea, and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' drops O from OCEAN to leave CEAN; 'in' puts TACE inside it. 'Whale's' reads as 'whale is', but it is the definition as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Cetacean is the adjective for whales, dolphins and porpoises, the order Cetacea.

clue.text: Fine to ignore most substantial witness

indicators.note: to ignore means to leave out, so the letter for fine is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: fattest means thickest, most substantial
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A judge rules it fine to ignore the most important witness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' removes F from FATTEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness, to declare under oath that something is true.

clue.text: Welsh associate seen around English coastal feature

indicators.note: seen around means placed on both sides of, so the friendly Welsh word wraps the letter for English

parts.note: bach is a Welsh term of affection for a friend or mate

explanation.surface: A Welsh friend is spotted near an English seaside landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: BACH is a Welsh word for 'friend' or 'dear'. BEACH is in the theme too: Amy Beach was an American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach is the sandy or pebbly shore, a typical feature of a coastline.

clue.text: Former President First Lady left in bed

indicators.note: in puts the first woman and left inside the word for bed

parts.note: a roost is a place to sleep, a bed, as for birds
Eve, in Genesis the first woman

explanation.surface: A former US President's wife, the First Lady, has left the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like a President's wife, Eleanor Roosevelt, but here it is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt were both Presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Endless charity around University provided by student group and former student

indicators.note: provided by means the student group is added next, after the first part
around means the trimmed charity word goes either side of the letter for university
endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor
the NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK

explanation.surface: A charity at a university, backed by a student group, is helped by an old graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last letter of the charity word, and 'around' wraps it round U. The NUS is Britain's National Union of Students; 'provided by' adds it after.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a graduate or past pupil of a school or university.

clue.text: Amount of land about to be held in a restricted zone?

indicators.note: to be held in means placed inside, so the word for about goes into the cage

parts.note: a cage is an enclosed, restricted space
re means about, concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A piece of land is going to be fenced off as a restricted area.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a cage is a playful sense of a restricted zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an area measured in acres, so it is a quantity of land.

clue.text: African country rejected adopting second religion

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the turned country takes the letter for second inside
rejected means turned back, so the country's name is read backwards

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: An African nation turned down a second faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses MALI to ILAM, and S goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith of Muslims, founded on the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: I will be embraced by not entirely virtuous woman

indicators.note: will be embraced by means the letter I goes inside the shortened word
not entirely means the word is not complete, so it loses its last letter

parts.note: moral means virtuous, good

explanation.surface: Someone says they will be hugged by a woman who is not entirely good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims MORAL to MORA, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Moira is a female first name, so in crosswords it can be clued simply as a woman.

clue.text: Stop couple over imprisoning blokes? That's something settled

parts.note: end means stop, finish

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding inside, so the reversed number wraps the men
over means turned over, so the word for couple is read backwards

parts.note: a couple is two
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: Stopping a couple jailing some men is a matter resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the couple word round to OWT, and 'imprisoning' sets the blokes between its W and T. 'Something settled' is a legal sense: money settled on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is money or property settled on a person or institution, as in a legal settlement.

clue.text: Succeeded bracketing old lady — as this?

definitions.text: Succeeded bracketing old lady — as this?

indicators.note: bracketing means enclosing as brackets do, so the word for succeeded goes round the mother

parts.note: won means succeeded, triumphed
old lady is slang for mother, so MA

explanation.surface: Someone did well while looking after an elderly lady, as a woman might.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: 'as this?' asks the solver to see that the old lady, a mother, is herself an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother, the old lady, is a female adult, so the clue describes one instance of the answer.

clue.text: Main canal with actual rocks? Here's aid for sailors

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters of the three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The sea and a canal with real rocks: here is something to help those at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like the sea, a fitting surface for sailors, but here it is only letters. 'rocks' rearranges MAIN, CANAL and ACTUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical almanac is a yearly book of tables of tides and star positions used for navigation at sea.

clue.text: Agitated point about university insignia? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: about would normally put the point around the other parts
quite the reverse swaps the containing roles, so university and insignia go round the point instead

parts.note: arms are heraldic insignia, a coat of arms
a pin has a sharp point

explanation.surface: A protestor is making a fuss about a university's coat of arms, or maybe the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, 'point about university insignia' wraps the point round the rest; 'Quite the reverse' swaps the roles, so the university and insignia letters wrap the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is an idiom for being angry and protesting, highly agitated.

clue.text: Name your old stone, expressing name — this stone?

indicators.note: expressing means pressing out, squeezing out, so the letter for name is pushed out of the opening words

parts.note: thy is the old form of your
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: An instruction to name your old gemstone, saying its name, and asking if this is it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressing' means squeezing out, not speaking: N is pressed out of NAME THY to leave AMETHY. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds, ST for short.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple variety of quartz used as a gem, so it is one such stone.

clue.text: Note working in wool will absorb time

indicators.note: will absorb means take in, so the letter for time goes inside the needlework word

parts.note: crochet is needlework that makes fabric from yarn or wool with a hook

explanation.surface: Knitting a note in wool will take a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will absorb' puts T inside CROCHET.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note worth one beat, called a quarter note in America.

clue.text: End of working week — almost ready — behold meat in sauce

parts.note: Fri, short for Friday, the last day of the working week

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ready is British slang for cash, as in ready money
behold means see, look

explanation.surface: At the end of the working week, almost done, look at the meat in its sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of working week' looks like it asks for a final letter, but it is FRI, short for Friday. 'almost' cuts CASH to CAS; 'ready' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricassee is a dish of pieces of meat stewed and served in a thick white gravy.

clue.text: Contractor perhaps avoiding fish in European country

indicators.note: avoiding means steering clear of, so the fish is removed from the worker

parts.note: a freelance is a self-employed worker on contract, one kind of contractor
an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A contractor perhaps avoids eating fish in a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' takes EEL out of FREELANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a large nation of western Europe with Paris as its capital.

clue.text: Biblical character: Uriah's first encountered in identical line

indicators.note: encountered in means met inside, so the opening letter goes into the word for identical

parts.note: same means identical

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Uriah is taken

explanation.surface: A Bible figure, Uriah, first appeared in the same line of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: SAMUEL also belongs to the theme: Rhian Samuel is a Welsh composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel was the Hebrew prophet who anointed Saul and David, with two Old Testament books named after him.

clue.text: Note a bit of meat, cut, will do for Mexican dish

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word for a bit of meat loses its last letter

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat on the bone

explanation.surface: A short note says a piece of meat, cut up, will serve for a Mexican meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like part of the butchery, but it trims CHOP to CHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip topped with cheese and other fillings, a Tex-Mex snack.

clue.text: What gets some pets excited: roughly rising quantity of milk?

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly, about

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: milk is delivered or bought by the pint

explanation.surface: A quantity of milk going up roughly is what excites some pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses PINT to TNIP. In Britain milk has long been sold by the pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Catnip is a plant of the mint family whose scent makes many cats playful and excited.

clue.text: A sport for men releasing energy repeatedly? Something mixed on offer here

indicators.note: releasing means letting go, so the energy letter is dropped

parts.note: a male thing is for men
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: repeatedly means the same energy letter is dropped again from the next word

parts.note: a game is a sport

explanation.surface: A men's sport that wears them out again and again: something mixed is available here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport for men' gives MALE GAME; 'releasing energy repeatedly' drops both Es.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a mixture or blend, originally an alloy of mercury with another metal.

clue.text: Excellent energy party picked up

parts.note: go means energy, vigour

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the word for party is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: An excellent, lively party was collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' here is a reversal, turning DO into OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Good is a common term of approval meaning fine, of high quality, very satisfactory.

clue.text: Girl's recalled quote from free-thinker

parts.note: her means belonging to a girl

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for quote is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A girl took back a quote from a radical thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses CITE to ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds views against official doctrine, someone who thinks independently.

clue.text: Indian city right to the fore in Indian music

indicators.note: to the fore means brought to the front, so the letter for right moves forward

parts.note: Agra is the city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: An Indian city's music puts the right side to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the fore' moves the R of AGRA to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic pattern used as the framework for improvisation in Indian classical music.

clue.text: Arrivals bearing a lot of mail for writers

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the arrivals word holds the shortened mail word

parts.note: comers are people who arrive

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the word for mail loses its last letter

parts.note: post means mail

explanation.surface: New arrivals carry a big bundle of letters for the authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' takes all but the last letter of the mail word, and 'bearing' has the arrivals carry it. 'writers' means writers of music, the puzzle's theme being women composers.
explanation.definitionFit: Composers write music, so they are writers of scores.

clue.text: Forbidding end to obscene filth

parts.note: grim means stern, forbidding

indicators.note: end to means the last letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A ban to stop obscene dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: GRIME is a theme answer too: Helen Grime is a Scottish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime is dirt ground into a surface, a layer of filth.
